title: Split-horizon TTL jitter causing intermittent hostname flapping across dedicated tenants
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Customer escalation: in the last 72 hours multiple Dedicated tenants reported intermittent resolution of their private hostnames resolving to other tenants' endpoints after VPC-peering failover and autoscaler events. Impact was spiky — calls occasionally routed to a different tenant's internal proxy, causing authentication mismatches and data-plane errors. This ticket tracks the investigation, root cause remediation, short-term mitigation, and rollout of a durable fix to prevent recurrence.
steps_to_reproduce: Simulate a peering swap between two dedicated-VPCs while concurrently triggering horizontal scale-down of worker pools.
Run a high-query-rate workload that exercises egress path selection and name resolution (internal resolver -> peered resolver -> external fallback).
Observe cached A/AAAA and SRV entries in in-path resolvers and ephemeral NAT mappings on the returning client connections.
Run tcpdump on worker egress to capture DNS responses during failover window and compare TTL values and source resolver IPs.
investigation_notes: Observed TTL variance for split-horizon records served by the peered resolver pair: one side returned TTL=30s, the other returned TTL=300s depending on which resolver answered during the peering swap.
Ephemeral NAT port reuse combined with short TTLs led to a window where cached A records mapped to endpoints no longer owned by the original tenant after reparenting of routes.

Control-plane reconciliation delayed re-binding of tenant hostnames to new egress metadata for ~45s in several reproductions; this overlapped with short TTL responses and caused resolver cache to serve stale answers.
Customer-visible errors: 401/403 and mismatched TLS SNI when requests reached a different tenant's proxy; some requests succeeded after retry due to cache expiry.
Relevant logs: grafana dashboards show DNS query spikes and increased 5xx rates for the affected tenants between 2026-02-25T23:10Z and 2026-02-26T01:05Z.
decision_log: Short-term mitigation: set uniform split-horizon TTL floor to 120s for dedicated peering view to reduce jitter and extend cache consistency during peering transitions (approved 2026-03-01 by SRE lead).

Long-term fix: implement atomic host-binding reconciliation event that performs a proactive cache invalidation (EDNS flush) across our internal resolvers and triggers targeted resolver probe to prime correct records post-peering-change (design approved 2026-03-04).

Fallback policy: if reconciliation cannot complete within 90s, route tenant traffic to isolated fallback pool (no shared proxies) to preserve tenant isolation — temporary until reconciliation completes.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (hotfix) - 2026-03-03: apply TTL floor on dedicated peering view via resolver config change (canary in region us-west-2, 1% of tenants). Monitor for stabilization for 12h.

Phase 1 (reconciliation mechanism v1) - 2026-03-07: deploy control-plane hook that emits host-binding-change events and triggers targeted cache flush on resolvers. Start with non-customer-critical namespaces.
Phase 2 (safety routing) - 2026-03-09: enable automatic fallback to isolated proxy pool when reconciliation exceeds 90s. Roll forward on success, rollback if error rate rises >2x.
Phase 3 (global rollout) - 2026-03-12: enable for all Dedicated tenants after verification window and postmortem sign-off.
test_plan: Unit tests for host-binding reconciliation logic and resolver flush API client.
Integration test simulating peering swap + autoscaler scale-down with synthetic workload validating no cross-tenant resolution for 10k queries/minute.
Chaos test: random network partition between control plane and resolver fleet while reconciliation runs to validate fallback triggers.
Post-deploy: run targeted validation script across 50 customers to confirm hostname to tenant mapping remains consistent for 5 minutes across repeated peering toggles.
rollback_plan: If hotfix TTL change causes unexpected latency or cache amplification issues, revert resolver TTL floor and re-open emergency incident; immediate step is to enable safety routing to isolate tenants.
If reconciliation deployment causes increased DNS error rates >1% absolute, immediately disable reconciliation worker and revert control-plane hook.
